recentWorks.title: Angular distribution of zeros of analytic quadrinomials and related harmonic polynomial and rational functions
recentWorks.abstract: An angular distribution of zeros of four-term complex-valued harmonic polynomial and rational functions is obtained by first showing that it is the same as that of a corresponding analytic quadrinomial, and then deriving zero inclusion sectors for such quadrinomials. Examples illustrate the theory.

recentWorks.title: A Note on Zero Inclusion Sectors for a Family of Harmonic Rational Functions
recentWorks.abstract: Zero inclusion sectors are obtained for a family of complex valued harmonic rational functions. The zeros of a limiting case are obtained explicitly.

recentWorks.title: Zero exclusion sectors for polynomials whose coefficients exhibit a +/-/+ sign pattern
recentWorks.abstract: The zeros of polynomials whose coefficients exhibit a +/-/+ sign pattern are sometimes excluded from sectors in the complex plane. It is shown how to obtain such sectors, as well as the number of zeros that lie between the sectors, along with bounds on their magnitudes. The results are illustrated with an application to polynomial eigenvalue problems.

recentWorks.title: Full-scatter vector field analysis of an overmoded and periodically loaded cylindrical structure for the transportation of THz radiation
recentWorks.abstract: Highly overmoded and periodically loaded structures, such as the iris-line waveguide, offer an attractive solution for the efficient transportation of diffraction-prone THz pulses over long distances (hundreds of meters). This paper presents the full-scatter field theory that allows us to analytically derive all the spectral (modal) coefficients at the discontinuities of the iris line. The spectral analysis uses vector fields, superseding scalar field descriptions, to account for diffraction loss, polarization effects, and ohmic loss on practical conductive surfaces. recentWorks.abstract: In this note, we report observations on the growth trends of diffraction power loss and ohmic power loss, as functions of screen thickness, in highly overmoded THz or mm-wave iris-line waveguides that are constructed from finitethickness screens. Recent theoretical developments have given a detailed field description, including eigen and transient analyses, that characterizes such waveguides under paraxial dipole-mode excitation. recentWorks.title: Rethinking data infrastructure and its ethical implications in the face of automated digital content generation
recentWorks.abstract: Recent AI developments have made it possible for AI to auto-generate content—text, image, and sound. recentWorks.title: An information-matching approach to optimal experimental design and active learning
recentWorks.abstract: The efficacy of mathematical models heavily depends on the quality of the training data, yet collecting sufficient data is often expensive and challenging. Many modeling applications require inferring parameters only as a means to predict other quantities of interest (QoI). Because models often contain many unidentifiable (sloppy) parameters, QoIs often depend on a relatively small number of parameter combinations. recentWorks.abstract: Engineering students often face challenges designing digital tools for underserved communities due to limited understanding of local user contexts, particularly in cross-cultural and remote settings. This study addresses that gap through a case study: the NicaAgua App, which started as a senior design project by computer engineering students for climate forecasting for smallholder farmers in Nicaragua. recentWorks.title: Mobile Application to Distribute Water Quality and Weather Information in Rural Nicaragua
recentWorks.abstract: The ability to access accurate information about water quality and weather is something that many people take for granted, but in small, rural communities in northern Nicaragua this information is not easily accessible to everyone. Currently, weekly in-person meetings are held to distribute information such as water quality, weather conditions, and other important agricultural updates to the communities. recentWorks.title: Secure and Private Structured-Subset Retrieval: Fundamental Limits and Achievable Schemes
recentWorks.abstract: This work introduces the \emph{Secure and Private Structured-Subset Retrieval (SPSSR)} problem. In SPSSR, a user wishes to retrieve one subset from an arbitrary family of size-$D$ subsets from $K$ messages replicated across $N$ non-colluding servers that share randomness unknown to the user. The privacy requirement ensures that no server learns which subset is requested, while the security requirement ensures that the user learns nothing about the messages outside the requested subset. recentWorks.title: Private Structured-Subset Retrieval
recentWorks.abstract: We introduce the \emph{Private Structured-Subset Retrieval (PSSR)} problem, where a user retrieves $D$ messages from a database of $K$ messages replicated across $N$ non-colluding servers, and the demand is restricted to a known structured family of $D$-subsets. This formulation generalizes Multi-message Private Information Retrieval (MPIR) and captures settings where the demand space is constrained by application-specific structure. recentWorks.title: Private Contiguous-Block Retrieval
recentWorks.abstract: We introduce the \emph{Private Contiguous-Block Retrieval (PCBR)} problem, where a user retrieves a block of $D$ messages with contiguous indices from $K$ replicated messages stored across $N$ non-colluding servers, while hiding the identity of the requested block from each server. This problem is motivated by storage and streaming systems where files are split into ordered segments. The process involved the freezing of CNF and urea suspension followed by immediate thawing in the microwave. A slow freezing rate produced a uniform pore structure, whereas fast freezing using liquid nitrogen resulted in the aggregation of CNF upon thawing. recentWorks.title: LeMon: An eBPF-Driven System Monitoring Framework for Wireless Access Points
recentWorks.abstract: Wi-Fi has become the primary connectivity medium for modern consumer and IoT devices, yet performance and reliability issues remain poorly understood due to a lack of efficient real-time monitoring tools. Existing approaches rely on coarse Access Point (AP) portal logging, kernel modifications, or packet capture, all of which impose significant overhead or lack sufficient visibility into the network stack. In this paper, we present LeMon, an eBPF-based monitoring framework that performs high-rate, in-kernel aggregation of network statistics and exports them to user-space through a lightweight …

recentWorks.title: DAFRA: Demand-Aware Fair Rate Allocation to Flows on Commodity Switches
recentWorks.abstract: Modern cloud data centers and edge clusters run on fabrics built from commodity, fixed-function switches. In such environments, particularly when AI and non-AI workloads coexist, flows with diverse rate demands share the same network. Consequently, demand-aware fair allocation at the bottleneck egress ports of switches is required to ensure that flows receive bandwidth proportional to their offered load, subject to link capacity. Existing mechanisms, including heterogeneous end-host congestion control and coarse switch policers, ignore demand-proportional targets and together cause persistent …

recentWorks.title: Cross-Layer Performance Analysis of P-EDCA
recentWorks.abstract: Modern Wi-Fi applications require tight latency bounds and predictable throughput, and they rely on a mix of transport protocols (e.g., TCP Cubic, BBR, New Reno, and UDP) whose performance is highly sensitive to MAC-layer behavior. The forthcoming 802.11bn amendment introduces Prioritized EDCA (P-EDCA) to reduce latency for high-priority traffic, yet its crosslayer impact on transport performance remains insufficiently understood. Diverse viral GPs from both DNA and RNA viruses-including VSVG, HSV-gpB, SARS-CoV-1 spike, and RD114A-are shown to efficiently incorporate into sEV membranes in human cells, independent of viral assembly. recentWorks.title: Intracellular trafficking governs membrane scaffold performance in small extracellular vesicle engineering
recentWorks.abstract: Small extracellular vesicle (sEV) scaffold performance depends on intracellular trafficking. VSVG, ACY and FAR enable robust cargo loading through endosomal trafficking, establishing a trafficking-guided framework for rational nanotherapeutic design.

recentWorks.abstract: High-precision stabilization of inertially stabilized gimbal systems is heavily challenged by nonlinear friction and structural resonances. To address this, this paper proposes an Extended Dynamic Mode Decomposition (EDMD) approach based on Koopman Operator Theory to represent the nonlinear dynamics in a high-dimensional linear state space. To resolve the unmeasurability of the lifted states, a Linear Quadratic Gaussian (LQG) controller is designed, and the associated loss of robust stability margins is successfully reconstructed via Loop Transfer Recovery (LTR). recentWorks.title: Model-Based Koopman-Galerkin Lifting for Guaranteed H-Infinity Output Feedback Control of Nonlinear Systems
recentWorks.abstract: In this paper, we present a model-based Koopman-Galerkin framework for output-feedback control of nonlinear systems with known dynamics. With a suitable actuator augmentation, the finite-dimensional realization preserves the actuator dynamics and the constant input matrix. The approach is based on an exact decomposition of the lifted dynamics into an LTI system and a finite-order closure residual. It also applies to non-control-affine systems and allows dictionaries that do not span an invariant subspace.
